interpŏlātĭo , ōnis, f. id.,
I.an alteration made here and there (post-Aug.): “tenuatam (chartam) curiosa interpolatione, principalem fecit e plebeia,” by a curious dressing made the best paper from common, Plin. 13, 12, 23, § 75 ; Tert. adv. Haer. 39.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
